items.bold: IRAN DELIVERED UPDATED PROPOSAL to US via Pakistan. Brent fell 3% to $108.17 on news.
items.text: CNBC (9 hours ago) and Rigzone (8 hours ago) confirmed: Iranian state news agency IRNA reported Friday that Tehran delivered a new/updated proposal to the US via Pakistan. Pakistani officials separately confirmed to MS NOW that mediators received an updated proposal from Iran and it has been delivered to the US. Brent crude fell nearly 3% to settle at $108.17 per barrel on the news — WTI fell 3% to $101.94. Markets priced in partial optimism that a deal may still be possible. However, Trump said: "Iran wants to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it. Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left." IRNA did not elaborate on what the proposal contained — no details on Hormuz or nuclear. Content remains unknown.

items.bold: CENTCOM prepared plan for "SHORT AND POWERFUL" wave of strikes — Axios. US pitching allies on joint naval force.
items.text: Rigzone (citing Bloomberg and Axios, 8 hours ago) confirmed: CENTCOM has prepared a plan for a "brief wave of strikes" — described separately by Axios as "short and powerful" — to break the negotiating deadlock with Iran. Trump was briefed Thursday by both CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper AND Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Dan Caine — two of the most senior US military officials simultaneously. Bloomberg separately confirmed: the US is pitching allies on a joint naval force to secure the Strait of Hormuz. This is the first confirmed report of a multinational naval force being actively pitched — building on the 30-country Northwood conference (April 22-23) that planned a post-deal Hormuz reopening force. The dual track — new Iran proposal (diplomatic) + CENTCOM strike plan (military) — means both sides are positioning simultaneously.

items.bold: IRAN activated air defenses around TEHRAN Thursday — counter to reconnaissance drones.
items.text: Bloomberg confirmed (Rigzone citing Bloomberg): Iran activated air defenses around the capital Tehran late on Thursday to counter reconnaissance drones. The cause and the drones' origin are unconfirmed. This is a significant development — reconnaissance drones over Tehran suggest pre-strike intelligence gathering is active. Combined with CENTCOM's "short and powerful" strike plan preparation, the Tehran air defense activation signals Iran's military is on high alert for a potential resumed US-Israeli strike. The timing — the night after Trump's CENTCOM military briefing — is not coincidental. Iran is tracking US strike preparation signals and responding with active air defense posturing.

items.bold: Trump: "Not satisfied — they want a deal because they have no military left." Ghalibaf defiant.
items.text: CNBC confirmed: Trump told reporters Friday: "Iran wants to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it. Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left." Trump maintained the blockade will continue. Simultaneously, Rigzone (citing Bloomberg) confirmed Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf posted on X: "Good luck blockading a country with those borders" — referring to Iran's large size and long land borders that make a complete blockade difficult. Iran is maintaining its classic dual-track posture: diplomatic (new proposal delivered) + public defiance (Ghalibaf mocking the blockade). Iran's IRNA confirmation that a new proposal was delivered without any details on content signals Iran wants credit for diplomatic engagement without committing to terms publicly.

items.bold: Democrats: war cost "less than half — maybe less than quarter" of Pentagon's $25B. Murkowski AUMF May 11.
items.text: Claims Journal (12 hours ago) confirmed: Democrats challenged the Pentagon's stated $25 billion war cost figure during Thursday's Senate hearing with Hegseth. One unnamed senator said the actual cost was "probably less than half, maybe less than a quarter, of the total cost of war." Defense Secretary Hegseth maintained the 60-day war powers clock "pauses" during the ceasefire. Democrats disputed this legal interpretation. GOP Sen. Murkowski announced plans to introduce an Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF) measure when the Senate returns from recess the week of May 11 — if the White House does not present a credible plan. The Murkowski AUMF deadline is the next domestic US political pressure point on the war.

military.t: CENTCOM Prepared "Short and Powerful" Strike Plan. US Pitching Allies on Joint Naval Force.
military.d: Rigzone (citing Bloomberg and Axios, 8 hours ago) confirmed two major military developments: (1) CENTCOM has prepared a plan for a "short and powerful" wave of strikes to break the negotiating deadlock — the clearest US military strike preparation signal since the ceasefire. Trump was briefed Thursday by both Admiral Brad Cooper (CENTCOM) AND Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Dan Caine simultaneously. (2) The US is actively pitching allies on a joint naval force to secure the Strait of Hormuz — the first confirmed active allied recruitment for a multinational naval force. This builds on the 30-country Northwood conference (April 22-23) that planned post-deal Hormuz reopening. A joint naval force would be different — it would enforce freedom of navigation actively, potentially against Iranian vessels. Gulf Arab states, UK, France, and Australia are likely candidates being pitched.

military.t: Iran Activated Air Defenses Around TEHRAN Thursday — Counter to Reconnaissance Drones.
military.d: Bloomberg confirmed (Rigzone citing Bloomberg): Iran activated air defenses around the capital Tehran late on Thursday to counter reconnaissance drones. The cause and drones' origin remain unconfirmed. The timing is significant: this activation occurred the night after Trump's joint CENTCOM + Joint Chiefs briefing, suggesting Iran is monitoring for pre-strike intelligence signals and responding. Reconnaissance drones typically precede strike planning — they map air defense systems, communications infrastructure, and target sites. Iran's air defense activation over Tehran (a politically and militarily sensitive signal) suggests the IRGC believes a US strike may be imminent and is positioning defensively. Combined with the IRGC Aerospace Command's "long and painful strikes" threat and Mojtaba's "bottom of the waters" statement — Iran is in active military alert mode despite continuing the diplomatic track.

military.t: Trump: "Not Satisfied — They Want a Deal Because They Have No Military Left." Ghalibaf Defiant.
military.d: CNBC confirmed: Trump told reporters Friday: "Iran wants to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it. Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left." Blockade continues. The "no military left" claim is disputed — CBS News confirmed last week that US officials with knowledge of intelligence said Iran maintains more military capabilities than the White House or Pentagon has publicly admitted. Rigzone (Bloomberg) confirmed Ghalibaf simultaneously posted on X: "Good luck blockading a country with those borders" — mocking the blockade's reach. Iran is maintaining its dual track: diplomatic (new proposal delivered) + public defiance (Ghalibaf mocking blockade) + military alert (Tehran air defenses activated). This is Iran's consistent pattern: engage diplomatically while projecting maximum public defiance.

military.t: Democrats: War Cost 4x+ Pentagon's $25B. Murkowski AUMF May 11. War Powers Clock Disputed.
military.d: Claims Journal confirmed: during Thursday's Senate hearing with Hegseth, Democrats challenged the Pentagon's stated $25 billion war cost figure — one unnamed senator said the actual cost was "probably less than half, maybe less than a quarter." Hegseth maintained the 60-day war powers clock "pauses" during ceasefire. Democrats disputed this legal interpretation. Sen. Murkowski (R-Alaska) confirmed AUMF coming week of May 11 if no credible WH plan. War Powers Act legal debate: some lawmakers say 60-day clock started Feb 28 (deadline: April 29 — already passed); others say the clock started from Congressional notification (deadline May 1). Others say ceasefire days don't count. The legal ambiguity benefits the Trump administration for now — but Murkowski's AUMF threat will crystallise the debate by mid-May.

assessment.headline: DAY 64, 9AM SAT: IRAN DELIVERED NEW PROPOSAL via Pakistan — Brent fell 3% to $108. Trump: "Not satisfied." CENTCOM has "short and powerful" strike plan. US pitching allies on joint naval force. Tehran air defenses activated. India Monday = cautious positive open.
assessment.body:
Saturday 9 AM IST. Day 64. Iran moved diplomatically. The US military moved simultaneously.

IRAN'S NEW PROPOSAL — WHAT WE KNOW
• IRNA (Iran state news) confirmed Friday: Tehran delivered updated proposal to US via Pakistan
• Pakistani officials confirmed separately: mediators received it; delivered to the US
• Content: UNKNOWN — IRNA gave no details on Hormuz or nuclear
• Brent fell 3% to $108.17 on the news — markets priced partial optimism
• Trump: "Iran wants to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it"
• Trump: "Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left"
• This is Iran's third formal submission since the war began

THE SIMULTANEOUS US MILITARY TRACK
• CENTCOM prepared "short and powerful" strike plan — Axios confirmed
• Trump briefed Thursday by Cooper (CENTCOM) AND Dan Caine (Joint Chiefs Chair)
• US pitching allies on joint naval force to secure Hormuz — Bloomberg confirmed
• Tehran air defenses activated Thursday night — counter to reconnaissance drones
• The two tracks (diplomatic + military) are running simultaneously
• Iran delivering a proposal while Tehran tracks US reconnaissance drones

IRAN'S DUAL POSTURE
• Diplomatic: new proposal delivered to Pakistan → US
• Military: air defenses activated; IRGC Mousavi "long and painful strikes" threat
• Public: Ghalibaf "Good luck blockading a country with those borders"
• Supreme Leader: "Americans at bottom of Gulf waters" — permanent Hormuz doctrine
• Classic Iran pattern: maximum pressure on all fronts simultaneously

INDIA MONDAY 9:15 AM IST
• Brent $108 (down from $114-126 range) = partial relief
• Iran proposal = cautious optimism
• CENTCOM strike plan = tail risk remains
• Morgan Stanley: Sensex 95,000 December 2026
• HDFC Securities: markets near end of 18-month correction cycle
• Net: cautious positive Monday open likely
• Nifty: support 23,800-24,000 / resistance 24,400-24,600
• OMC hike: less imminent at $108 vs $121-126 peaks — but not cancelled
• Rupee Rs 95.32 ATL — RBI intervention expected

THE WEEK AHEAD
• Iran proposal content: unknown — Trump response timing unknown
• Murkowski AUMF: week of May 11 if no credible WH plan
• Joint naval force pitching: ongoing — Gulf Arabs, UK, France, Australia
• War Powers 60-day legal debate: continuing
• Tehran air defense activation: requires monitoring

VERDICT: Day 64 opens with the war's most diplomatically constructive signal in two weeks — Iran delivered a new proposal — but the most militarily alarming signal simultaneously: CENTCOM has a "short and powerful" strike plan ready and the US is pitching allies on a joint naval force. Iran knows this too — it activated air defenses around Tehran the night Trump got the briefing. The diplomacy and the military tracks are now running in parallel at maximum intensity. The week of May 11 is the next hard deadline — Murkowski's AUMF will crystallise Congressional authority over the war.
